newsitem.title: UK: Crown Leisure seeks London stockmarket listing.
newsitem.headline: Crown Leisure seeks London stockmarket listing.

text.p: Crown Leisure, a slot machine and video game business, said it has applied for a full listing on the London stock exchange.

The company is Britain's fifth biggest operator and second largest seller of coin-operated amusement machines. Government deregulation of the amusement industry in June has given the company a significant fillip.

The authorities allowed the introduction of up to two amusement with prizes (AWPs) machines in licensed betting offices, an increase of two to six jackpot machines in casinos, while member clubs and bingo halls are allowed a maximum of three and four machines respectively.
Deregulation also introduced 10-pound all-cash prizes, whereas previously the maximum was eight pounds in tokens on AWPs, which has greatly increased consumer interest in the machines.
The group reported pretax profit of 1.4 million stg on turnover of 26.7 million stg in the last yera.
Crown is expected to raise between five and seven million stg to be used to reduce debt and fund expansion.
Dealings in the new shares should start in mid-December, said Crown in a statement.
